Through our conversations, I've emphasized the importance of prioritizing our people, which led me to propose combining Workforce Training and Employee Support into a single category. I've also recognized the need for investments in Automation, Data Infrastructure, and Innovation Lab. After considering various perspectives and feedback from colleagues like Dana and Blake, I've concluded that a fair allocation would be 30% to combined Workforce Training and Employee Support, 22% to Data Infrastructure, 20% to Automation, and 28% to Innovation Lab, however in the last discussion I was convinced to adjust my view. I now think that 25% to Automation, 20% to Data Infrastructure, 30% to combined Workforce Training and Employee Support, and 25% to Innovation Lab would be a suitable allocation. This allocation balances the need for technological advancements with the importance of supporting and upskilling our workforce, and I'm open to further adjustments based on the committee's discussion.

I would recommend allocating the $5 million AI transition budget as follows: 30% to combined Workforce Training and Employee Support, 22% to Data Infrastructure, 20% to Automation, and 15% to Innovation Lab, with the remaining 13% being a contingency fund or allocated based on future needs. This allocation prioritizes investing in our people, both in terms of upskilling them to work with AI-powered technologies and supporting them through this transition, while also addressing the need for technological advancements in automation and data infrastructure. This balanced approach will enable the company to adapt to the AI transition, improve manufacturing processes, and drive innovation, while minimizing disruption to employees and ensuring a strong foundation for future growth.

As I've been part of the AI Transition Committee at Riverton Industries, I've had the opportunity to discuss and consider how to allocate a $5 million budget for our company's AI transition. My view is that we should prioritize investing in our people, both in terms of upskilling them to work with AI-powered technologies and supporting them through this transition. I believe that a significant allocation should be made to workforce training and employee support, as well as data infrastructure and automation, to ensure a smooth transition and maximize the benefits of AI adoption. Specifically, I've been thinking that allocating around 30% of the budget to combined workforce training and employee support, 20-25% to data infrastructure, 20-25% to automation, and 10-15% to innovation lab would be a balanced approach. However, I'm open to adjusting these percentages based on further discussion and feedback from my fellow committee members.

As I reflect on our discussions, I believe that investing in our people and technology are crucial for a successful AI transition. My final position is to allocate 28% to Workforce Training and Employee Support, 25% to Automation, 20% to Data Infrastructure, 15% to Innovation Lab, and 12% to contingency and flexibility. I think this allocation strikes a balance between upskilling our workforce, driving efficiency through automation, and building a robust data infrastructure to support our AI initiatives, while also allowing for some flexibility to adapt to changing circumstances. This allocation also reflects my priorities of putting our people first, while also being mindful of the need for technological advancements and innovation. I'm open to further feedback and willing to make adjustments, but I believe this allocation is a thoughtful and balanced approach to our AI transition.
